documents.title: H&P - Admission, Acute COPD Exacerbation
lines: HPI:
77 y/o male with severe COPD (GOLD D, FEV1 32% predicted 8 mo ago) presents to ED at 01:20 with 3 days of worsening dyspnea, cough, thick yellow sputum.
Symptoms began after grandson had a head cold. Has been using home albuterol MDI q2h without relief.
Sleeping in recliner x2 nights. No fever reported at home. No chest pain, no orthopnea, no leg swelling.
Uses home oxygen 2L continuously; required 5L NC in the ED to maintain target saturation.
Baseline: ambulates 20 feet to bathroom with walker, dyspneic at rest on bad days. Last admission 5 mo ago for same.
Past Medical History:
COPD with chronic hypercapnia, prior intubation once (2 admissions ago), cor pulmonale, HTN, type 2 DM, GERD, 50 pack-year smoking, quit 4 yrs ago.
Home Medications:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg BID
Pantoprazole 40 mg daily
Furosemide 20 mg daily
Allergies: sulfa (rash)
Social: lives with wife in single-story home. Daughter nearby, checks in daily. No alcohol. Oxygen concentrator at home with 50 ft tubing.
ED Course:
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing; remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.
Physical Exam:
Vitals 03:05: T 37.1, HR 108, BP 148/82, RR 32, SpO2 89% on 4L NC.
Gen: ill-appearing elderly male, sitting forward at edge of bed, anxious.
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
HEENT: pursed-lip breathing, no JVD appreciated at 30 degrees, mucous membranes dry.
Chest: barrel-shaped, hyperresonant, diffuse expiratory wheeze bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, poor air movement at bases.
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, PMI not palpable.
Abd: soft, nontender, mild hepatomegaly.
Ext: trace bilateral ankle edema, no calf tenderness, nails with mild clubbing.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no asterixis, no tremor.
Labs:
WBC 13.2, Hgb 14.8, Plt 244
Na 137, K 4.4, Cl 95, HCO3 31, BUN 22, Cr 1.1, glucose 188
Lactate 1.6, BNP 142, troponin <0.02 x1
Respiratory viral panel sent, sputum gram stain: mixed flora, few PMNs
Imaging/ECG:
CXR portable: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation, no effusion, no pneumothorax.
ECG: sinus tachycardia 108, poor R wave progression, no acute ischemic change.
Assessment/Plan:
77 y/o male with severe COPD, acute exacerbation with acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure, likely viral trigger.
1. Resp failure - continue BiPAP 14/6, wean to 4L NC as tolerated, target SpO2 88-92%. RT at bedside. Repeat ABG in AM.
2. COPD exacerbation - albuterol-ipratropium neb q4h scheduled plus q2h prn; continue inhaled maintenance once off BiPAP.
3. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
4. Abx - azithromycin 500 mg IV x1 then 250 mg daily, day 1 of 5.
5. DM - hold metformin, q4h POC glucose, insulin sliding scale as above.
6. Prophylaxis - enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.
7. Goals of care - pt states he would accept short-term intubation if needed; wife aware. Full code for now.
Admit to stepdown unit. Attending notified at 03:40.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: Subjective:
Pt slept in short stretches overnight. Reports breathing is easier this morning. Now speaking in longer phrases without pausing.
Tolerated BiPAP well; mask off at 12:30 yesterday after 9 continuous hours, back on overnight at 22:00.
Coughing up moderate yellow sputum, less tenacious. Denies chest pain. Appetite poor but took some breakfast.
Objective:
Vitals: T 36.9, HR 92, BP 136/78, RR 22, SpO2 91% on 3L NC.
Overnight glucose readings 342 at 20:00, 214 at 00:00, 168 at 04:00. Received 10 units regular insulin total per sliding scale.
Gen: more comfortable, sitting up in chair, no tripod posture this morning.
Chest: scattered expiratory wheeze, improved air entry bilaterally, no rales.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Ext: trace edema unchanged.
Neuro: alert, oriented, no asterixis.
Labs: WBC 10.1, Cr 1.0, K 4.1, HCO3 30.
Repeat ABG 06:20 on 3L: pH 7.36, PaCO2 52, PaO2 66.
Viral panel positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus.
Assessment/Plan:
Acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure secondary to COPD exacerbation, improving.
1. Continue nocturnal BiPAP tonight if remains inpatient; day on NC, wean toward home 2L.
2. Continue albuterol-ipratropium nebs q4h; resume tiotropium and budesonide-formoterol today.
3. Transition to prednisone 40 mg PO daily today, total 5-day course.
4. Continue azithromycin day 2 of 5.
5. Glucose - continue q4h POC and sliding scale while on steroid; expect improvement as steroid tapers off.
6. PT eval for ambulation with pulse ox.
7. Ambulate with RN this afternoon on 2-3L, check exertional sats before considering discharge.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: Subjective:
Pt reassessed at 14:40. Ambulated 100 feet in hallway with walker accompanied by PT.
Reports dyspnea 3/10 with walking, back to baseline by his report. Wife present and agrees he looks like himself.
No nocturnal BiPAP needed for daytime; off BiPAP since 06:00.
Objective:
Vitals at rest 14:45: HR 88, BP 130/74, RR 18, SpO2 92% on 2L NC.
Ambulation: SpO2 nadir 89% on 2L at 100 feet, recovered to 92% within 90 seconds of rest.
POC glucose 12:00 was 182, 16:00 pending.
Chest: minimal end-expiratory wheeze, good air movement, no accessory muscle use.
No tripod positioning. Speaking full phrases, no pauses.
Ext: trace edema. Neuro: intact.
Assessment/Plan:
COPD exacerbation improved; now at home oxygen requirement of 2L continuously with stable exertional saturations.
1. Cleared for discharge home this evening.
2. Continue prednisone 40 mg PO daily to complete 5 days total; azithromycin to complete 5 days.
3. Resume home inhalers; RN to re-teach MDI technique with spacer before discharge - done at 15:20, pt demonstrated correctly.
4. Restart metformin at home; daughter to check fingersticks BID until steroid course done given glucose spike this admission.
5. Home oxygen 2L continuous, concentrator already in place; counseled not to increase above 3L without calling.
6. COPD action plan given, rescue inhaler refilled.
7. Follow-up with primary care in 5 days, pulmonary in 3 weeks.
8. Return precautions reviewed with pt and wife: worsening dyspnea at rest, confusion, drowsiness, fever.
Discharge summary and medication list to be completed at 17:00.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD2
lines: Admitting diagnosis: Acute COPD exacerbation with acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure.
Discharge diagnoses: COPD exacerbation (rhinovirus/enterovirus), steroid-induced hyperglycemia, chronic hypoxemic respiratory failure on home O2, HTN, T2DM.
Length of stay: HD1 to HD2, discharged HD2 evening.
Brief Hospital Course:
77 y/o male with severe COPD presented at 01:20 with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and purulent sputum after a viral exposure.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Uses home oxygen 2L continuously; required 5L NC in the ED to maintain target saturation.
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing; remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.
IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale.
Azithromycin started for purulent sputum, planned 5-day course. CXR without consolidation. Troponin negative, ECG with sinus tachycardia only.
By HD2 morning repeat ABG on 3L showed pH 7.36, PaCO2 52, PaO2 66. Weaned to 2L NC, his home flow rate.
Ambulated 100 feet with walker on 2L with SpO2 nadir 89%, prompt recovery. Steroid transitioned to oral. Cleared for discharge.
Discharge Exam:
HR 86, BP 128/76, RR 18, SpO2 92% on 2L NC. Minimal end-expiratory wheeze, no accessory muscle use, alert and oriented.
Discharge Medications:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily x2 more days to complete course
Azithromycin 250 mg PO daily x3 more days
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID with spacer
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Lisinopril 10 mg daily, metformin 500 mg BID, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, furosemide 20 mg daily
Oxygen: 2L continuous via home concentrator
Follow-up:
Primary care in 5 days for symptom and glucose check.
Pulmonary clinic in 3 weeks with spirometry.
Fingersticks BID at home until prednisone finished; call if readings persistently above 300.
Pulmonary rehab referral placed.
Return precautions: dyspnea at rest not relieved by rescue inhaler, confusion, drowsiness, fever above 38.3, need for oxygen above 3L.
Pt and wife verbalized understanding of plan. Discharged home with daughter at 18:10.
